# Django-Bolt

> Django-Bolt serves typed API routes from a Django project with a Rust HTTP server (Actix Web and Tokio, called through PyO3). It validates and encodes with msgspec. The Django ORM, admin, auth, settings and apps keep working. Handlers are typed `async def` or `def` functions, in the style of FastAPI and Django Ninja. Bolt is not a WSGI or ASGI application: `python manage.py runbolt` is the server in development and in production, with no gunicorn or uvicorn. Routing, authentication (JWT, API keys), guards, CORS and rate limits run in Rust before Python starts. Compression of the response also runs in Rust.

Key facts:
- Install: `pip install django-bolt`. Add `"django_bolt"` to `INSTALLED_APPS`. Write `api.py` with `api = BoltAPI()` and `@api.get(...)` handlers. Run `python manage.py runbolt --dev`. OpenAPI docs are at `/docs`.
- Supported Python and Django versions: see https://bolt.farhana.li/intro/install/ (the source of truth is the `pyproject.toml` classifiers).
- Measured: 324,493 requests per second for a small JSON route, with 8 processes, 100 connections, AMD Ryzen 5 5600G, bombardier over loopback (2026-09-19). With one process each and the same PostgreSQL data, 2.8x Litestar and 5.8x FastAPI on a 1 KB JSON response (2026-08-30). Always quote the conditions with a number.
- Validation is msgspec, not Pydantic. Use `msgspec.Struct` or the Bolt `Serializer`.
- Django middleware does not run on Bolt routes by default. Turn it on with `BoltAPI(django_middleware=True)`.
- Version 0.x. A minor release can change an API. MIT license.
- Repository: https://github.com/dj-bolt/django-bolt · PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/django-bolt/ · Docs: https://bolt.farhana.li/
